title: Weak and dissipative solutions for the Hasegawa-Mima equation
summary:
We consider the Hasegawa-Mima equation in its ``Euler-like'' velocity form: \[\partial_t(u-Δ^{-1}u)+(u\cdot
abla)u-u^\perp\log n_0=0,\] $n_0$ being the time-independent function appearing in the particle count $n=n_0e^{ rac{e\varphi}{T}}$, and $u$ being the drift velocity $
abla^\perp\varphi=-
abla\varphi	imes\hat z$. Adapting the notion from Lions' book on the Euler equations, we prove the existence of dissipative solutions for this equation for any $L^2$ divergence free initial condition $w\in L^2(D)$, for $D=\mathbb T^2$ and $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ a bounded $\mathcal{C}^1$ domain.
